title: Evaluation-normalized geometric nearby-cycle duality
statement:
Use $A=A_{E,n}$, the algebraically closed field $k$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and the trait $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$, its strict henselization and geometric generic point $\bar\eta$ of [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $\mathcal T$ be any separated finite-type $D$-scheme. On small etale sites write $R\Psi_{\mathcal T}=i^*Rj_*$ as in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange]. For $v=0,\bar\eta$ put $\omega_v=Ra_v^!A$, where $a_v:\mathcal T_v\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ is the structure map, and put $D_vL=R\mathcal Hom_A(L,\omega_v)$, using the constructible exceptional adjoints and derived tensor--Hom operations of [def-trf-admissibility] and [def-trf-dualizing-complex], interpreted over the indicated separably closed residue fields. For every bounded constructible finite-Tor etale complex $L$ on $\mathcal T_{\bar\eta}$, the canonical map
$$R\Psi_{\mathcal T}(D_{\bar\eta}L)\longrightarrow D_0(R\Psi_{\mathcal T}L)$$
is an isomorphism. The map meant here is the tensor--Hom transpose of
$$R\Psi(D_{\bar\eta}L)\otimes_A^LR\Psi L\longrightarrow R\Psi(D_{\bar\eta}L\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{R\Psi(\operatorname{ev}_L)}R\Psi\omega_{\bar\eta}\longrightarrow\omega_0,$$
where the first arrow is the lax tensor map and the last is the exceptional nearby-cycle comparison for the structure map, normalized by $R\Psi_DA=A$.

For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ and the projection $q:T_{\bar\eta}\to T$, the canonical geometric-field-base-change comparisons $q^*\omega_T\cong\omega_{T_{\bar\eta}}$ and $q^*D_TM\cong D_{T_{\bar\eta}}q^*M$ are isomorphisms for $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and identify the evaluation pairings. Thus these comparisons use relative dualizing objects over the two fields, without a trait-dimension shift.

source.place: §4.1.4(b), axiom (V), citing Illusie, Autour du theoreme de monodromie locale, Theorem 4.2; relative duality normalization in §§0.2, 1.3.1--1.3.2

proof.text: Work on small etale sites throughout, with relative dualizing objects over the two geometric residue fields. Write $\alpha_X$ for the displayed evaluation transpose in the statement. The operation-square lemma supplies this actual arrow (not a choice of an abstract duality isomorphism) and its proper, smooth, reduction, and finite-trait-extension compatibilities. Pass to the strict henselization of $D$. In the induction below allow every excellent strictly henselian finite extension of this trait, so alteration and descent stay in the class. The same argument also proves the assertion for all bounded constructible complexes; this broader intermediate domain is necessary for the kernels in the resolutions. Descend each geometric generic input, and each finite-type etale generator as it occurs, after a finite extension of the generic field; the finite-extension square then identifies the geometric comparisons. Thus the generator reductions can be performed on actual generic fibres.

Let $C_X(L)=\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha_X(L))$ on the functorial derived models. Induct on $d=\dim X_{\bar\eta}$, allowing non-pure-dimensional $X$ and all bounded constructible $L$. If the geometric generic fibre is empty both terms are zero. If $L$ is supported on a closed subscheme of generic dimension less than $d$, write it as the closed pushforward of its restriction; the proper square identifies its cone with that closed pushforward of the lower-dimensional cone, hence with zero. Vertical components likewise carry no generic input. Reduction is harmless by the same operation-square lemma. Thus all errors supported on a generically nowhere-dense closed subset can be discarded at this stage.

source.place: Agent dimension induction; compare Lu--Zheng proof of Theorem 5.1

proof.text: For this fixed $d$, use a second induction on the lower cohomological degree of $C_X(L)$ for $L\in D_c^{\leq0}$. The uniform-range lemma starts it at a fixed integer (take a lower bound for the two functors, minus one for their cone). The resolution lemma gives a triangle $u_!A_U\to L\to Q_{<0}\to$, with $Q_{<0}$ concentrated in degrees $\leq-1$. Contravariance shifts the cone bound of $Q_{<0}$ up by one. Thus, if the cone bound $\geq n$ holds for all inputs, proving that it is $\geq n+1$ on the free etale generators proves it for all inputs. Repeat for every $n$; this proves vanishing, since an object with no cohomology in any integer degree is zero. No finite resolution, finite global dimension of $A$, or thick generation by constant sheaves is used.

source.place: Agent degree induction using uniform bounds and free-etale resolutions

proof.text: Reduce a free generator to proper integral constants. Compactify $X$ over the trait as $X\subset\overline X$, then compactify the descended separated finite-type map $U\to\overline X$ as $U\xrightarrow eP\xrightarrow h\overline X$, with $e$ open and $h$ proper. Replace $P$ by the reduced closure of $U$. Etale local-dimension preservation gives $\dim U_\eta\leq d$; the dimension--transcendence-degree formula at generic points gives the same bound for each component of $P_\eta$, since its dense open has the same generic residue field. A proper closed subset of an irreducible finite-dimensional component has smaller dimension: append that component to any chain of irreducible closed subsets. Thus $P_\eta\setminus U$ has dimension less than $d$ componentwise. Localization compares $e_{\eta!}A_U$ with $A_{P_\eta}$, and the outer induction discards the boundary. The proper square, $Rh_{\eta*}e_{\eta!}A_U=Ru_!A_U$, and restriction to $X_0$ reduce the generator comparison to $\alpha_P(A)$. Finally $A_P\to\bigoplus A_{P_i}$ for the reduced irreducible components is an isomorphism away from their intersections. Those intersections are proper closed subsets componentwise; the same dimension argument and localization discard the kernel and cokernel on the generic fibre. Proper squares for the closed components reduce to integral proper constants. Components of generic dimension below $d$ are already covered.

source.place: Agent double-compactification and localization reduction for etale generators

proof.text: For an integral proper total scheme dominating the trait, take a plurinodal alteration after a finite trait extension. Handle the reduced generic components separately as in Step 4. On one component write $h:P\to X$ for the alteration. Shrink to a dense open $U$ on which $h$ is finite, and apply generic finite splitting. Etale locally on a further dense open, $h_U$ is a nonempty disjoint union of universal homeomorphisms. Topological invariance identifies $h_{U*}A$ there with a finite product of copies of $A$; summing these copies is invariant under their permutation on overlaps, so the maps glue to a surjection $h_{U*}A\to A_U$. The index set is nonempty because $h$ is dominant and proper. Put $j:U\to X$. The maps $j_!h_{U*}A\to Rh_*A_P$ and $j_!A_U\to A_X$ are isomorphisms on $U$; their cones have smaller generic-dimensional support, and the outer induction kills their comparison cones. The degree induction permits the kernel of the surjection $j_!h_{U*}A\to j_!A_U$: its comparison cone is shifted up by one. It therefore suffices to prove $\alpha_X(Rh_{\bar\eta*}A)$ invertible, which the proper square reduces to $\alpha_P(A)$. No degree is divided out.

source.place: Agent alteration reduction within the degree induction

proof.text: Prove the constant-coefficient assertion on a plurinodal tower by its length. Length zero is the trait: its geometric fibres are points, their relative dualizing objects are $A$, and $R\Psi_BA=A$ by the unit normalization. The tensor--Hom transpose of the multiplication pairing $A\otimes_A A\to A$ is the identity of $A$. Hence $\alpha_B(A)$ is invertible, with no shift or twist from the dimension of the trait.

source.place: Agent point normalization of the plurinodal induction

proof.text: For a positive-length tower write its last stage as a projective nodal curve $f:P\to Y$. The generic dimension of $Y$ is $d-1$. By the outer induction, $\alpha_Y(A)$ is invertible, and so is $\alpha_Y(Rf_{\bar\eta*}A)$: proper direct image is bounded constructible by nearby finiteness and the operation-square domains. The proper square gives $Rf_{0*}C_P(A)=0$. On the smooth locus $V$ of $f$, the smooth square identifies $C_P(A)|_{V_0}$ with $f_0^*C_Y(A)(1)[2]$, which is zero. Therefore $C_P(A)$ is supported on the closed nonsmooth locus, finite over $Y$ by the plurinodal lemma. Finite-support conservativity now gives $C_P(A)=0$. This proves the constant comparison on the tower, completing Step 5, the degree induction, and the dimension induction.

source.place: Agent nodal-curve induction and finite-support detection

proof.text: Every bounded constructible complex on the chosen geometric generic fibre descends after a finite extension, and the operation-square lemma identifies its evaluation comparison after this change. Apply Steps 1--7 on that extension and transport the resulting isomorphism back to the fixed geometric fibres. In particular it applies to the bounded constructible finite-Tor $L$ in the item. Nearby finiteness ensures its image remains in the stated finite-Tor domain. Because each induction used the canonical $\alpha$ and equalities of arrows, the isomorphism obtained is exactly the transpose of the lax tensor--evaluation--structural-counit composite in the question.

For the field-extension assertion define $\delta_T:q^*\omega_T\to\omega_{T_K}$ and $\beta_T(M):q^*D_TM\to D_{T_K}q^*M$ by compact-support base change, the structural counit, and evaluation, as in the operation-square lemma, with $K=\kappa(\bar\eta)$. Prove $\beta_T(M)$ invertible by the dimension and degree inductions of Steps 2--5 over algebraically closed fields: the free-etale resolutions and uniform lower bounds apply verbatim, the double compactification and localization of Step 4 reduce to proper integral constants, and the local sum construction of Step 5 reduces those constants to their smooth proper alterations. Proper and open squares identify the maps at every reduction. Here dimension means the dimension of the field-scheme and no change of trait is involved.

On a smooth pure-dimensional alteration $P/F$ of dimension $r$, normalized purity in the operation-square lemma makes $\delta_P$ the identification $q^*A_P(r)[2r]=A_{P_K}(r)[2r]$. For the constant input $A_P$, the evaluation transpose $\beta_P(A_P)$ is exactly this map, so it is invertible. The field induction of Step 9 proves $\beta_T(M)$ invertible for every bounded constructible $M$, hence in particular for the stated $M\in D^b_{ctf}$. Taking $M=A_T$ and using $D_TA_T=\omega_T$ gives invertibility of $\delta_T$ as well. These objects are dualizing relative to the fields; there is no use of a dualizing object relative to the one-dimensional trait.

source.place: Agent smooth-purity base case over fields

proof.text:
Finally, the definition of the tensor--Hom transpose gives the equality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{q^*M}\circ(\beta_T(M)\otimes1)=\delta_T\circ q^*(\operatorname{ev}_M),$$
using the canonical tensor comparison for inverse image. Thus the two invertible field comparisons identify the specified evaluation pairings. The same transposition identity was built into $\alpha_T$ in Step 1, so this also verifies the evaluation normalization of the nearby-cycle isomorphism, rather than just an isomorphism of its source and target.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the axiom-(V) citation in §4.1.4(b), using an alteration/degree induction; Lu--Zheng §§3,5 supply the intended supporting references, local PDF WANTED.

from.place: Proof (1) and (2), specialization to the normal cone: §4.1.4(b), axiom (V), citing Illusie, Autour du theoreme de monodromie locale, Theorem 4.2; relative duality normalization in §§0.2, 1.3.1--1.3.2

split_report.summary: Evaluation-normalized proof by generic-dimension and cohomological-degree induction; plurinodal alteration, nodal-curve finite-support detection, and a separate field-extension induction. Four independent statement-only inputs retain the missing non-elementary claims.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the nearby-duality input for specialization in proof (1)--(2) of lem-trf-local-term-locality, through lem-trf-trace-specialization and lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison.

tool_uses.why: Compactify total schemes and extend etale generators; generic geometric tool, no alternative unit route.
Detect the nodal-curve comparison cone on finite nonsmooth support; no duality assertion is used.
Generic splitting of a finite alteration on a dense open; the resulting trace epimorphism is constructed by sums in Step 5.
Topological invariance identifies the universal-homeomorphism sheets with constant etale sheaves; used only as a generic tool in the same trace construction.
Etale generators have generic dimension at most that of their target; a generic geometric dimension tool, not a replacement of the specialization route.
Taking a reduced closure of a dense generic open does not change component dimension, because the generic residue field is unchanged; no node of this unit states the dimension formula.
